title: Start and end every run with run.py
decision: Run `run.py start` first, `run.py check` after writing outputs, and `run.py finish` last. Do not reply that the work is complete until `finish` exits with code 0.
reason: Scripted start and end make the checks always run and let hooks know whether a run is active. The definition of done does not differ between agents.
how: scripts/run.py. finish exits with code 1 when the contract checks fail
good: Reply with the text printed by `run.py finish` after it exits with code 0
bad: Reply "done" right after writing the outputs

title: Do not change the skill's own files during a run
retired: It got in the way of small fixes by the user

title: Ask questions before start
decision: Ask the user everything before `run.py start`. If a question becomes necessary after start, run `run.py wait --question <question>` first. When asking is impossible, use the default and list it under "Values decided by default" in the report.
reason: If agents differ on whether to ask mid-run, the outputs differ. wait prevents hooks from blocking the turn that asks the question.
how: scripts/run.py start exits with code 3 and prints the questions when a value that must be asked is missing. wait pauses the hooks
good: Ask the questions printed by start (exit code 3), then rerun start with the answers in `--set`
bad: Ask the user about the format after writing half of the output

title: Use the check hooks only to check outputs and protect the run record, never to block input or changes to the skill
decision: While this skill is running (status: active), the output-check hooks do only two things: check outputs after an edit and before the turn ends, and deny direct edits to the run record (`.skill-runs/<name>/state.json`, `report.md`) with edit tools. When it is not running, they do nothing. They never block changes to the skill's own files or hook settings, and never block or rewrite what the user says. Without hooks, `run.py check` and `finish` perform the same output checks.
reason: What is constrained is the AI's output, not the user's input or small fixes to the skill, and sessions that do not use this skill are left alone. If the AI rewrites the run record directly, the check baseline and the report can no longer be trusted.
how: scripts/hook.py. install.py registers it for Claude Code (.claude/settings.json) and Codex (.codex/hooks.json)
good: The Stop hook sends the agent back until the checks pass
bad: A UserPromptSubmit hook rejects requests written in an unexpected way

title: Reply with the finish text unchanged
decision: Reply with the text printed by `run.py finish` unchanged. Do not add text before or after it and do not summarize it. When the run is aborted, reply in the same way with the text printed by `run.py abort`. Before finish, write anything that could not be decided to `.skill-runs/<name>/notes.md` as bullets starting with "- " (up to 10); finish puts them under "## Notes".
reason: The form and content of the report do not differ by AI. Readers always see the values decided by default and the check results.
how: scripts/run.py finish and abort build the text and save it to .skill-runs/<name>/report.md. check and finish validate the form of notes.md
good: Write an undecided default to notes.md as a "- " bullet and reply with the finish text unchanged
bad: Summarize the finish text and append free-form notes
